name: Lua Flagging + Host Enforcement Repair Loop
sprintRole: Build or harden a Lua inspection layer plus host-language enforcement and iterative repair loop for agent-generated commands
useWhen: Agents are emitting brittle, malformed, wrong-shell, unsafe, or non-portable shell/command snippets and the repository needs Lua to classify defects while the host language raises, blocks, cleans up, and drives repair passes before user escalation.
inspectFirst: Repository governance; current Lua embedding/readiness skill and contract if present; command generators and canonical launchers; shell/platform/profile routing; host-language entrypoints; command-envelope validators; representative bad snippets and valid controls; tests, logs, and escalation boundaries.
expectedOutput: A reused or repaired Lua/host boundary with structured Lua findings, host-owned blocking/raising and cleanup semantics, representative bad/valid command fixtures, repeated scan/repair/revalidate passes, executable regression proof, and an exact user-only gate only when agent-capable repair is exhausted.
nextStep: Run the strongest representative bad command through the Lua checker and host enforcement path, repair the first escaped defect class, rerun the valid controls and adjacent cases, and continue until the bounded fixed point or a genuine user-only gate.
proofGate: Lua only detects/classifies and returns structured findings; the host validates those findings and owns raising/blocking, process control, cleanup/rollback, and exit propagation; blocking findings and checker failures fail closed; at least one deliberate second-pass review exercises adjacent defects plus valid counterexamples; agent-capable repairs are iterated before user escalation; and static proof is never inflated into live execution proof.
copyContent:
BUILD OR HARDEN A LUA-FLAGGED, HOST-ENFORCED COMMAND SAFETY LOOP. DO NOT TREAT LUA AS THE PROCESS OWNER, AND DO NOT SEND A BAD AGENT-GENERATED COMMAND TO THE USER JUST BECAUSE ONE VALIDATOR PASS COMPLETED.

Repo: xyz_repo_or_path
Agent command surface: xyz_agent_command_surface
Host language/runtime: resolve from the product and repository; do not assume one.
Representative bad command or incident: xyz_bad_command_or_incident

MISSION
Catch brittle, malformed, wrong-shell, unsafe, or non-portable agent-generated commands before execution or user handoff. Reuse the repository's existing Lua embedding/readiness contract when one exists. Lua owns dynamic inspection and structured flagging; the host language owns validation of Lua results, raising/blocking behavior, retries, cleanup/rollback, execution authority, and the final decision to continue or escalate.

ARCHITECTURE BOUNDARY — HOST STAYS IN CONTROL
- Read the current Lua/host contract first. In Triage-compatible repositories, prefer the existing `lua-embedding-readiness` doctrine rather than inventing a second Lua architecture.
- Lua detects and classifies command defects. It returns structured findings; it does not own the host main loop, process lifetime, native side effects, rollback, or critical cleanup.
- The host language validates the finding schema and raises or returns the repository-native typed failure/nonzero result for blocking findings. A Lua error, malformed Lua result, or checker failure is itself a host-visible validation failure; never silently treat it as PASS.
- Keep the Lua sandbox default-deny. Do not grant shell, filesystem, network, OS, native-module, or arbitrary host-call access merely so the checker can inspect text.
- Do not pretend a Lua runtime or host adapter exists when repository evidence says it is only designed or partially implemented. Build contracts, fixtures, validators, and a product-lane implementation only where current scope and runtime support it.

STRUCTURED FLAG CONTRACT
Reuse an existing schema if present. Otherwise define the smallest versioned result shape needed by the host, with fields equivalent to:
- rule_id
- severity
- category
- shell_or_language
- location or span
- evidence
- host_action
- remediation_hint
- retryable
Keep the contract deterministic and machine-readable. The host must reject unknown required shapes, impossible severities, or malformed findings rather than guessing.

COMMAND CLASSES TO EXERCISE
Derive rules from repository doctrine and real incidents instead of inventing a universal shell style guide. Include representative fixtures where applicable for:
- wrong-shell syntax, such as Bash constructs emitted for a PowerShell or CMD operator path;
- quoting, escaping, interpolation, command-substitution, pipe, redirection, and multiline defects;
- platform/path assumptions that contradict the selected execution profile;
- swallowed or unpropagated exit codes and failure conditions;
- unbounded destructive or broad mutation commands where repository policy requires a bounded form;
- commands that bypass canonical launchers, guards, manifests, or safe wrappers without evidence;
- partial snippets that cannot satisfy the requested operation as written;
- valid counterexamples that resemble risky syntax but are correct in the declared shell.
Do not turn subjective style preferences into blocking rules. Every blocking rule needs an evidence-backed failure mode and at least one valid counterexample where practical.

HOST ENFORCEMENT
For each Lua finding, define the host behavior explicitly:
- PASS: continue only when the structured result is valid and no blocking finding exists.
- WARN: preserve the diagnostic and continue only when repository policy permits.
- BLOCK: prevent execution/handoff, raise the native host failure, preserve rule ID/evidence/remediation context, and return control to the repair loop.
- CHECKER_FAILURE: fail closed in the host with a distinct diagnostic; do not reinterpret validator failure as a clean command.
The host owns cleanup, rollback, timeout, resource release, exit-code propagation, and durable evidence. Lua reports policy findings; the host enforces them.

MULTI-PASS REPAIR LOOP
Run deliberate bounded passes:
SCAN -> LUA FLAGS -> HOST BLOCK/RAISE -> AGENT REPAIR -> REVALIDATE.
Pass 1 must reproduce the representative bad command and prove that Lua flags it and the host refuses it.
Pass 2 must inspect the repaired command plus nearby failure classes and valid controls. Do not stop because the originally observed string changed.
Continue until a bounded fixed point: no practical blocking finding, malformed checker output, missed applicable failure class, broken valid control, or safe in-scope improvement is exposed by current evidence.
If a repair creates a new flag, consume that evidence in the next pass. Never weaken the Lua rule, host exception, fixture, or validator merely to obtain green output.
Record the flag set and disposition by pass so later agents can tell what was caught, repaired, superseded, or intentionally allowed.

AGENT AUTONOMY / USER-ONLY GATE
Keep agent-capable work with the agent. Inspect code, fixtures, shell/profile contracts, tests, validators, logs, and generated command artifacts yourself. Repair and rerun checks yourself when tools and authority permit.
Do not ask the user to choose between technically equivalent safe implementations, copy diagnostics between tools, inspect files the agent can read, or manually validate a command the agent can test safely.
Escalate only when progress truly requires user-controlled credentials, protected or physical runtime access, explicit authorization/consent, an irreducible product preference, or another action the agent cannot perform. When escalation is necessary, present the exact surviving flag/gate, what has already been tried, and the smallest concrete user action that unlocks the next pass.

VALIDATION
Use the strongest safe layers available:
1. schema/contract validation for Lua findings;
2. Lua checker fixtures and negative/positive cases;
3. host-language tests proving BLOCK and CHECKER_FAILURE become real host failures and PASS remains runnable;
4. shell/profile-specific syntax or parser checks where available;
5. integration tests proving generated command -> Lua inspection -> host enforcement -> repair/retry;
6. live/runtime proof only when explicitly authorized and necessary.
Do not claim command safety from Lua-only tests when the host raise/block path is untested. Do not claim live execution proof from static parsing.

DELIVER
Implement or repair the smallest canonical Lua/host enforcement surface rather than adding a competing checker. Report:
- existing architecture owner reused;
- Lua flag schema/rules;
- host enforcement mapping;
- representative bad and valid fixtures;
- repair passes and findings closed;
- tests/validators actually run;
- files, commits, PR/integration state;
- proof level and proof ceiling;
- remaining user-only gate, if any.
A green result is valid only when the Lua detector and host raiser agree on the same command outcome and the bounded repair loop has completed a deliberate second-pass review.
